mechanism_claims.claim_text: RN3, RN6, and RN7 have the strongest membrane depolarization/permeabilization and reduced C. albicans survival in Table 3, supporting direct membrane-disruption activity rather than a generic antifungal label.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: RN1-RN8, strongest source-supported values for RN3/RN6/RN7
mechanism_claims.limitations: Mechanism strength is table/caption supported; exact plotted kinetic traces were not digitized because table values were sufficient for the gate.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper reports RNase3 peptide binding to C. albicans cells and beta-D-glucan, supporting cell-wall interaction as a direct source-located mechanism component.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Binding is shown for RNase3 peptide; do not generalize exact binding strength to every RN peptide.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: RN3 and RN7 peptides show DNA-binding gel-retardation evidence, supporting intracellular target affinity as a contextual mechanism claim.
mechanism_claims.limitations: DNA binding is mechanistic context; the paper does not prove DNA binding is the sole killing mechanism.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: RN3 and RN7 reduce C. albicans biofilm viability/mass and alter biofilm architecture in source-located biofilm assays.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: RN3 and RN7 peptides against established/early C. albicans biofilms
mechanism_claims.limitations: Biofilm figures support activity phenotype; exact values are retained only where figure captions/text provide them.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: qRT-PCR figures show RN3/RN7 treatment changes C. albicans planktonic and biofilm gene expression, including cell-wall/biofilm-related genes, as downstream response context.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: RN3 and RN7 treatment of planktonic cells and biofilms
mechanism_claims.limitations: Gene-expression changes are downstream response evidence and should not be promoted to a single direct lethal target.
